newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ILO censures 20 countries for labour violations.
newsitem.headline: ILO censures 20 countries for labour violations.

text.p: The International Labour Organisation on Thursday censured 20 countries, including South Korea which it urged to recognise trade unions such as the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU).

In a report, the United Nations agency's freedom of association committee also denounced violence against trade unionists -- including murder, disappearances, and intimidation -- in Colombia, Nigeria and Sudan.

The report by the ILO's freedom of association committee, which held closed-door meetings in Geneva earlier this month, was adopted unanimously by the ILO's Governing Body late on Wednesday. Its 226-page report was issued on Thursday.
The committee oversees compliance with the fundamental principles of freedom of association, which guarantee the right of workers to organise and to engage in collective bargaining.

The ILO committee appealed to South Korea to allow it to make a high-level mission to ensure that recently announced revisions to its controversial labour law of last December are consistent with the principles of freedom of association.

In response to complaints against South Korea, filed by unions including the KCTU and the Korea Automobile Workers' Federation, the ILO urged the government "to take the necessary measures to render trade union pluralism legal without delay".
